sources.title: Structured interview source containing the matrix longest-increasing-path prompt
Deterministic, exhaustive and randomized matrix longest-increasing-path differential validation

claims.text: The preserved source asks only for the longest increasing path in a matrix; the four-direction, strict-increase, rectangular-input, null/empty and Java API behaviors are explicit candidate contracts rather than preserved source wording.
The candidate defines memo[r][c] as the longest strictly increasing four-direction path starting at cell (r,c), so each cell state is fully expanded once and then reused.

The executable validation compares the candidate against an independent value-sorted dynamic-programming oracle on deterministic cases, 840 exhaustive small matrices and 20000 seeded randomized matrices while checking empty and jagged-input contracts.

Under the explicit strict-increase contract, every directed move increases the cell value, so the state graph is acyclic; memoized DFS checks at most four outgoing neighbors per cell, giving O(mn) state work with O(mn) memo storage and worst-case O(mn) recursion depth.
